core_obligations: Contraction over an affine open (proof lines 4998-5010): let U be an affine open of the base containing the image of the curve; the contraction lemma over an affine base provides a contraction of the curve over U together with an ample invertible module on the target whose pullback is a twist of the given relatively ample module by a multiple of the curve.

Glue to a global contraction (proof lines 5010-5022): the target of the contraction and the complement of the curve in the source agree away from the exceptional point, so they glue to a scheme over the base; the contraction and the identity on the complement glue to a morphism which contracts the curve.

Recover properness and relative ampleness (proof lines 5022-5034): the preimage of the affine open is proper over it, while away from the image of the exceptional point the glued morphism agrees with the original one, so properness follows from localness on the base; the ample module over the affine open and the restriction of the original relatively ample module agree on the overlap and hence glue to an invertible module on the glued scheme, which is relatively ample because it is so over the affine open and away from the exceptional point.

Deduce the quasi-projective case (proof lines 5036-5042): write the quasi-projective source as an open subscheme of a projective one, apply the first part to the projective model and let the target be the image of the original source in the contracted model, which is open because the contraction is an isomorphism away from the curve; the resulting morphism is the required contraction and the target is quasi-projective as it carries a relatively ample invertible module by the construction above.
proof_roadmap: Contract the curve over an affine open containing its image and record the ample module on the target.
Glue the contracted piece with the complement of the curve and check properness by localness on the base.
Glue the invertible modules to get a relatively ample module, then reduce the quasi-projective case to the projective model.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that an exceptional curve of the first kind inside a fibre of a finite type morphism over a Noetherian base can be contracted while preserving projectivity, respectively quasi-projectivity, of the source over the base (statement lines 4985-4996). The proof (proof lines 4998-5047) contracts the curve over an affine open, glues the result with the complement of the curve, verifies properness by localness on the base and glues the invertible modules to obtain a relatively ample module, and reduces the quasi-projective case to a projective model. H2: a glueing argument with three inputs, written out in full.
